title: Situational Awareness Hedge Fund Lost 65% in Q3 2026
summary: Leopold Aschenbrenner's AI-focused hedge fund Situational Awareness lost 65% in Q3 2026 after highly levered bets on AI firms nearly caused implosion.
body_markdown:
**Officially launched on November 26, 2026.**


#### 💡 TL;DR


- Situational Awareness hedge fund lost 65% after fees in Q3 2026 following highly leveraged AI bets that triggered margin calls.
- The fund sold a major portion of its public equities portfolio to Citadel in July to avoid collapse during market volatility.
- Despite Q3 losses, the fund remained up 88.5% year-to-date through September with 70% public stocks and 30% private positions.


Situational Awareness, the AI-focused hedge fund led by Leopold Aschenbrenner, disclosed a 65% loss after fees in the third quarter of 2026, according to a Wall Street Journal report citing an investor letter. The dramatic decline followed highly levered positions in artificial intelligence companies that pushed the fund to the brink of collapse during July market turmoil.


## July Crisis and Portfolio Liquidation


The fund faced existential risk in July 2026 when a brief panic about AI valuations swept global markets, triggering margin calls from banking partners. To meet obligations and prevent complete implosion, Situational Awareness sold a substantial portion of its public equities holdings to Ken Griffin's Citadel. The forced liquidation marked one of the most visible casualties of the summer's AI market volatility.


Aschenbrenner, who founded the firm after publishing a viral 2024 essay on AI development timelines, had built a reputation for aggressive use of leverage to amplify returns on AI-related investments. That strategy delivered outsized gains during bullish periods but created severe vulnerability when sentiment shifted rapidly.


## Year-to-Date Performance and Current Holdings


Despite the third quarter collapse, Situational Awareness remained up 88.5% after fees for the year through September, demonstrating the magnitude of earlier gains. The fund's current portfolio composition stands at approximately 70% publicly traded stocks and 30% private company positions, according to the investor letter reviewed by the Journal.


The private holdings received a significant boost from the IPO of Anthropic, which represented the fund's largest private position. Aschenbrenner indicated the firm may rebalance away from Anthropic exposure, though he expressed strong bullishness at the IPO pricing level. The letter did not detail performance for October, when AI company valuations came under renewed scrutiny and further market swings complicated the investment landscape.


## Revised Risk Management Approach


In his communication to investors, Aschenbrenner acknowledged the painful lessons from the July near-collapse and outlined a more measured approach to portfolio risk. "Volatility, yes; existential risk, even if we are totally wrong, never," he reportedly wrote, signaling a shift away from leverage levels that could threaten the fund's survival during market dislocations.


The fund still sees substantial opportunities in the AI investment landscape with high potential returns, maintaining its core thesis about firms positioned to benefit from the artificial intelligence revolution. However, the new risk framework suggests future gains will come without the extreme leverage that characterized earlier periods.


## What This Means


The Situational Awareness quarterly disclosure offers a stark case study in the risks of leveraged concentration in a volatile sector. While AI investing has generated exceptional returns for early movers, the summer 2026 episode demonstrates how quickly sentiment shifts can threaten highly levered positions. For investors evaluating AI exposure, the fund's experience underscores the importance of position sizing, leverage limits, and liquidity management even in high-conviction themes. As AI markets continue to mature through boom-and-bust cycles, risk-adjusted returns may prove more sustainable than maximum leverage strategies.
